title: What fraction of the whole square is shaded?
description: A whole square is cut into four equal squares, and the shaded part sits inside one of them. The shaded part is found as a fraction of a fraction of a fraction, by multiplying one quarter, one half and three quarters.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shaded piece inside a piece inside a piece is found by multiplying the three fractions, each measured against the piece before it. Watch for students who give the shaded piece as a fraction of the small square and stop there.

source: Figure it Out (problems with fractions): what fraction of the whole square is shaded? The whole square is cut into four equal squares. In the bottom-right square, two lines run from its top corners to its centre and a vertical line goes down from the centre. The shaded part is the part left of the vertical line below the left line.
video_script.why: A learner finds a shaded piece as a part of a part of a part, multiplying the fractions as with the red square, the yellow triangle and the shaded piece.
video_script.substitution: the book's own whole square cut into four equal squares, with lines drawn in the bottom right one
video_script.anchor: a whole square cut into four equal squares, with lines drawn in the bottom right one and a shaded part inside it
video_script.payoff_line: Three thirty seconds of the whole square is shaded.

final_answer.spoken: three thirty seconds of the whole square

video_script.fraction_reading: one quarter, one half, one eighth, three quarters, one thirty second, four thirty seconds, three thirty seconds
maths_rules: the vertical line cuts it into two equal halves: left half = 1/2 x 1/4 = 1/8 of the whole
the left slanting line cuts a corner triangle off the top of the left half; its legs are half the side, so its area is 1/4 of the left half
shaded part = 3/4 of the left half = 3/4 x 1/8 = (3 x 1)/(4 x 8) = 3/32
video_script.design: The whole square on the left; the bottom right square is lifted out and enlarged, then the left half of it, then the shaded part inside that half.

narration: <bookmark mark='times'/>Step two, the vertical line cuts that square into halves.
The left half is a half times one quarter.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>One times one over two times four.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>That is one eighth of the whole square.

beats.on_screen: shaded part = 3/4 of the left half = 3/4 × 1/8 = (3 × 1) / (4 × 8)

The shaded part is three quarters of it.
<bookmark mark='times'/>That is three quarters times one eighth.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Three times one over four times eight.

It is one quarter times one eighth, which is one thirty second.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The shaded part and the triangle together must make the left half.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 3/32 of the whole square.  Check: 3/32 + 1/32 = 4/32 = 1/8
